correctness.rationale: For every commuting root-separable tuple, the coordinate Lagrange spectral idempotents form a complete orthogonal family. The explicit unitriangular element \(u=\sum_\alpha d_\alpha e_\alpha\) conjugates that family to its joint diagonal. Each strict comparable pair with unlike joint colors forces exactly one zero stabilizer coordinate, while like-colored pairs are free; the orbit has \(q^{b(c)}\) points. Expanding per-edge weights \(q+(1-q)\mathbf1_{\mathrm{equal}}\) yields the FK polynomial. Direct finite matrix enumeration passed 32 independently generated configurations. The theorem excludes nonsplit and inseparable polynomials.

originality.rationale: The novelty claim is the all-arity fixed-diagonal orbit census of commuting split-separable tuples over finite incidence algebras, its exact Potts–Tutte identification, and recovery of the two-variable graph polynomial from the algebraic counts. Earlier single-idempotent conjugacy, idempotent variety components, and standard Potts combinatorics are recognized as prior. Targeted searches did not locate an equivalent all-arity enumeration; a broader semisimple representation theorem may conceivably entail it, and independent priority review remains necessary.

value.rationale: The joint-diagonal orbit count is a complete exact distribution for an unbounded family of natural incidence algebra representation varieties; it shows that every all-arity tuple count depends only on the comparability graph, establishes recovery of the entire bivariate random-cluster/Tutte polynomial from these algebraic counts, and identifies a sharp chromatic/height degree threshold. This connects two independently motivated invariants rather than reporting an arbitrary finite instance or merely restating idempotent conjugacy.
